title: Country of the Month: Bulgaria
article:
Bulgaria is a small country in southwestern Europe bordered by Romania to the north, Serbia and North Macedonia to the west, Greece to the south, and Turkey to the southeast. Bulgaria encompasses a total area of 42,859.3 sq miles (110,993 sq kilometers) and has a population of 6.445 million.

The earliest inhabitants of Bulgaria were the Karanovo people (6500 BCE) who inhabited much of what is now known as Bulgaria. In the late 1300’s, the Ottomans conquered Bulgaria and made it into the center of the Rumelia or in English the “Roman Province.” In 1946, Bulgaria came under the control of the USSR as a socialist nation in the Eastern Bloc, an unofficial group of communist countries in Centrak and Eastern Europe.. Revolutions occurred in 1989 contributing to the transition from a socialist republic led by the Soviets, to a democracy. Bulgaria is a “unitary parliamentary system” composed of 28 provinces. A unitary perliamentry system where a single central government holds almost all the power.

Now in modern day Bulgaria has a GDP (gross domestic profit) of 107 billion USD. The GDP per capita is 17,000 USD and GDP per capita for PPP (a system that compares the amount of money to another currency typically USD) is 39,000 USD. Bulgaria’s GDP growth rate is 2.5% per year. Since 2007, Bulgaria's GDP has doubled. Bulgaria has a GINI of 37.2 which is in the middle but is still lower than the US’s GINI of 43. Bulgaria’s population of 6.445 million is composed of 84.6% Bulgarians, 8.4% Turks, 4.4% Roma, and 2.6% other. Most people in Bulgaria are Christian (64.7%),62.7%)are Bulgarian Orthodoxy and 2.0% other Christian.)) A large part of Bulgarians are irreligious (15.9%) and 9.8 % of Bulgarians are Muslim. Around .1% percent identify as some other religion and 9.5% are unanswered.

The geography of Bulgaria is very diverse with the Balkan mountains running through the center, and the Thracian plains to the south. The highest point in Bulgaria is Musala standing at a whopping 9596ft (2,925m) tall! Bulgaria is made up of many different climatic regions ranging from warm Mediterranean summers and to the coldfar south to tundra in the Balkan Mountains. Around 72% of Bulgarians reside in urban areas with the largest being Sofia, (the capital) with a population of 1.286 million people. Sofia is followed in size by Plodiv, with 126,563 people, Varna with 79.954 people, and Burgas with 44,449 people.

Some important historical sites in Bulgaria,is the Roman theatre of Plodiv which was founded in the 1st century AD. Another important site is the Tsarevets Fortress in Veliko Tarnovo. The fort served as the Second Bulgarian Empire’s primary fortress between the years of 1185 and 1393. What’s interesting about it is that the palace is on a hill that has been settled since the 2nd millennium BCE.
author: Sebastian Brodale
